bull_case: Zero Trust Exchange can become the control plane for users, workloads, branches and AI agents, displacing perimeter appliances and consolidating multiple security categories.
bear_case: Platform convergence from PANW, Cloudflare, Netskope and hyperscalers can commoditize parts of Zero Trust and force heavier selling and R&D spend.
thesis: ZS retains strong disruptive characteristics. Its cloud-native Zero Trust architecture directly replaces legacy hub-and-spoke firewalls/VPNs and is expanding into data security, AI security and SecOps. Adoption is already mainstream enough to produce multi-billion-dollar ARR.

evidence.claim: FY2026 ARR reached $3.771B, up 25%, while ex-acquisition ARR grew 20%.
Red Canary expands ZS into managed detection and response / Agentic SecOps.

counterevidence: Large competitors can bundle adjacent security products and subsidize platform adoption.
Organic ARR growth has moderated from earlier hypergrowth levels.
unknowns: Attach rates for newer AI-security and SecOps modules
falsifiers: If organic ARR growth falls to low teens while platform attach stagnates, disruption score should fall.
next_checks: Organic ARR growth excluding Red Canary

subscores.rationale: Cloud-native Zero Trust replaces perimeter architecture and materially changes security delivery economics.
Multi-billion-dollar ARR and 20% organic ARR growth demonstrate mainstream adoption.
Users, workloads, branches, data security, AI security and SecOps create multiple adjacent value pools.

uncertainties.rationale: Platform competitors increasingly offer comparable architecture.
